summary: This ASHA policy paper, developed by the Ad Hoc Committee on Service Delivery in the Schools and dated 1993, gives official guidance (not standards) defining communication disorders and variations. It defines communication disorders broadly and then specifies speech disorders (articulation, fluency, voice), language disorders (form, content, function), hearing disorders (deaf, hard of hearing), central auditory processing disorders, communication differences/dialects, and augmentative/alternative communication. The surrounding website navigation, sponsor logos and contact details are boilerplate and were ignored.
one_line: ASHA's 1993 policy paper defining communication disorders, including speech, language, hearing and central auditory processing disorders, and communication variations such as dialects.
key_facts: The 1993 ASHA paper 'Definitions of Communication Disorders and Variations' provides guidance that is not an official standard of the Association.
The guidelines were developed by the Ad Hoc Committee on Service Delivery in the Schools, with Frances K. Block as chair.
The 1992 guidelines superseded the paper titled 'Communication Disorders and Variations,' Asha, November 1982, pages 949-950.
A communication disorder is an impairment in the ability to receive, send, process, and comprehend concepts or verbal, nonverbal and graphic symbol systems.
A communication disorder may range in severity from mild to profound and may be developmental or acquired.
An articulation disorder is the atypical production of speech sounds characterized by substitutions, omissions, additions or distortions that may interfere with intelligibility.
A fluency disorder is an interruption in the flow of speaking characterized by atypical rate, rhythm, and repetitions in sounds, syllables, words, and phrases.
A voice disorder is characterized by abnormal production of vocal quality, pitch, loudness, resonance, and/or duration, inappropriate for an individual's age and/or sex.
A language disorder may involve the form of language (phonology, morphology, syntax), the content of language (semantics), and/or the function of language (pragmatics).
Deaf is defined as a hearing disorder that limits aural/oral communication performance so that the primary sensory input for communication may be other than the auditory channel.

Hard of hearing is defined as a hearing disorder, whether fluctuating or permanent, which adversely affects an individual's ability to communicate, with the auditory channel remaining the primary sensory input.
Central auditory processing disorders are deficits in information processing of audible signals not attributed to impaired peripheral hearing sensitivity or intellectual impairment.
Communication difference/dialect is a variation of a symbol system reflecting shared regional, social, or cultural/ethnic factors and should not be considered a disorder of speech or language.
Augmentative/alternative communication systems compensate for severe expressive and/or language comprehension disorders, temporarily or permanently.
